stories.headline: llama.cpp patches a remote code execution flaw in its network server
stories.summary: The llama.cpp RPC server cached compute graphs holding live memory pointers; freeing a buffer left those pointers dangling. An unauthenticated remote client could exploit the gap to leak memory addresses and hijack execution. Build b11000 discards cached graphs on buffer release. Patch before exposing llama.cpp's RPC port to any network.
stories.take: llama.cpp's networked inference server carried an unauthenticated remote code execution hole, now closed.

claims.claim: llama.cpp patches a remote code execution flaw in its network server
claims.summary_span: llama.cpp patches a remote code execution flaw in its network server
claims.source_span: rpc : invalidate cached compute graph when a referenced buffer is freed (#24292) ... yielding remote code execution.
claims.note: Source confirms a remote code execution bug in the RPC (network) server was fixed.

claims.claim: The llama.cpp RPC server cached compute graphs holding live memory pointers
claims.summary_span: The llama.cpp RPC server cached compute graphs holding live memory pointers
claims.source_span: The server caches the most recent compute graph per device so that GRAPH_RECOMPUTE can re-execute it without resending tensor data. The cached graph nodes hold direct pointers to backend buffers that were live at graph_compute() time.
claims.note: Source directly confirms the RPC server cached compute graphs with live memory pointers.

claims.claim: freeing a buffer left those pointers dangling
claims.summary_span: freeing a buffer left those pointers dangling
claims.source_span: If any of those buffers is later released via FREE_BUFFER, the next GRAPH_RECOMPUTE re-executes the cached graph through the dangling pointers (use-after-free).
claims.note: Source confirms freeing a buffer causes dangling pointers (use-after-free).

claims.claim: An unauthenticated remote client could exploit the gap to leak memory addresses and hijack execution
claims.summary_span: An unauthenticated remote client could exploit the gap to leak memory addresses and hijack execution
claims.source_span: The bug is reachable by an unauthenticated remote client. The dangling pointers point into chunks an attacker can reshape via subsequent ALLOC_BUFFER/SET_TENSOR commands, and the resulting read/write through the cached graph is sufficient to leak libc addresses and hijack the buffer iface vtable used by BUFFER_CLEAR, yielding remote code execution.
claims.note: Source confirms unauthenticated remote exploitation enabling memory leak and execution hijack.

claims.note: Source confirms build b11000 fixes the issue by discarding cached graphs in free_buffer().

stories.headline: Bias audits detect bias but cannot rank which model is least biased
stories.summary: Regulators use bias audit scores to rank models, but an arXiv preprint testing ten instruments across ten frontier models finds cross-tool rank agreement indistinguishable from chance (Kendall's W=0.07). Detection works; ranking doesn't. Raw responses and replication code are public. Before citing an audit score in vendor selection, which tool's construct actually matches your deployment?
stories.take: Bias audit rankings entered procurement criteria as settled scores; the ranking signal is noise.

stories.headline: Finetuning unlocks verbatim book recall that safety filters were supposed to block
stories.summary: An arXiv preprint shows finetuning GPT-4o, Gemini 2.5 Pro, and DeepSeek V3.1 on one author's work reproduces up to 85-90% of unrelated copyrighted books, with single spans exceeding 460 words. The same passages surface across all three providers. If your legal team cites alignment filters as a copyright defence, does that argument survive a finetuning audit?
stories.take: AI vendors' fair-use legal defences now rest on safety measures a finetuning step dissolves.

claims.note: The headline accurately paraphrases the paper's central finding that finetuning bypasses alignment/safety protections to unlock verbatim recall.

stories.headline: llama.cpp gains two sharper compression modes for Qualcomm chips

stories.headline: Small trusted judges outperform internal probes at catching AI lies
stories.summary: EleutherAI competed in Aletheia's Quest, a 19-team competition to build AI lie detectors. Their retrospective finds black-box monitoring generalised further than expected, while white-box probes inverted on out-of-distribution data. The companion repository, including a curated battery of deception datasets, is public on GitHub. Clone it before building any agent-monitoring eval stack.
stories.take: White-box probes were the assumed baseline; a 19-team competition found small black-box judges generalise further.

sections.synthesis: This week's practical releases each remove a different friction point rather than sharing a common theme, which is itself the signal: routing costs, on-device compression, SDK ergonomics, and lie-detection methodology are independent problems getting independent fixes. stories.headline: Safe agents can form unsafe systems, a 16-day stress test finds
stories.summary: An arXiv preprint ran eight parallel worlds of ten agents for 16 days, generating over 850,000 model calls. Three adversarial events — prompt injection, misinformation, and memory exposure — found no world fully resilient; threats written into persistent memory triggered actions up to 46 hours later. Threats persisting 46 hours later make the system the measurable unit of risk.
stories.take: Multi-agent safety evaluations targeted individual models; persistent shared memory makes the system the unit of risk.
